ground_ruling.why: the 6 pairs above are cf3d43a's per-8x8-tile R6 reading a 24 px wide sky element as a figure and asking the figure separation test (R1 body_ground, R2 same_hue_row, R3 white_blob) of a thing that stands on nothing. That reading is wrong on the facts, not only stale on the tool. The test that fits a sky element is R1b overlay_contrast, which asks that the ink OR the body clear 3:1 on every ground colour under it, and the cloud clears it on every one: on the sky $11 its body $20 reads 4.34:1, on the grey $00 it reads 3.93:1, and on the 5 white pixels its body is the ground colour at 1.00:1 while its ink $00 clears 3.93:1, which is what the or is for. The 5 white pixels in the crop (measured at 19,5 to 21,6 and 20,4 of the crop, 12 in the sky strip's own rows 80 to 95, and 0 in the parallax cloud layer) are the sky strip's own distant cloud tops, so a white crown over them is a cloud over a cloud, scenery meeting scenery, not a blob that has lost its edge. A figure test on that pair would fail it for sharing sky material with the sky.
